title: Musée Jacquemart-André opens Tintoretto's first career-spanning survey in France
summary: The Musée Jacquemart-André is showcasing the work of one of the leading figures of Italian Mannerism, Jacomo Robusti, known as Tintoretto (1518/19–1594). This exhibition presents, for the first time in France, a comprehensive overview of Tintoretto’s entire career and demonstrates how his artistic legacy has transcended temporal and geographic boundaries, establishing him as a key influence on 19th-century French painting. Jacomo Robusti, nicknamed ‘Tintoretto’ in reference to his father’s trade as a dyer, established himself as a major figure in 16th-century painting. In Venice, where he remained for all his life, his ambition found fertile ground. It was in this capital of culture that his remarkably long career unfolded. Although little is known about his training, he began making a name for himself in the late 1540s with prestigious commissions such as Miracle of the Slave (1548). title: Bertoia Auctions announces September 25 Mechanical Banks & Cast-Iron Toys auction
summary: Bertoia Auctions’ first major event of an active fall season will be a Mechanical Banks & Cast-Iron Toys Auction held on Friday, September 25, and headlined by the outstanding mechanical bank collection of the late Dr Robert E Booth, Jr (1945-2026). Dr Booth was renowned for assembling one of America’s finest private collections of Americana and folk art. Dr Booth’s extraordinary home – featured in the pages of Architectural Digest and Antiques magazine – reflected a lifetime of collecting at the highest level. While Dr Booth assembled collections in numerous categories, it is his mechanical banks that will be offered exclusively in the September sale. More than 100 rare, highly sought-after examples will be up for bid.

title: Design Week Lagos presents new generation Nigerian design talent at Paris Design Week 2026
summary: Design Week Lagos presents Athanasius Johnson, Adaora Enwonwu, Emma Emodi, Oluwakayinsade Ademuson, Joan Eric-Udorie, Myles Igwebuike and Richard Aina at Paris Design Week from 10-19 September, 2026. Together, the seven selected designers represent a new generation of designers whose work spans furniture, lighting, sculpture and collectible design, reimagining African craftsmanship, material innovation and cultural heritage through contemporary design. Paris Design Week brings together 500 participants across 320 venues – including showrooms, galleries, studios, museums, and exceptional locations – in the heart of Paris’s four iconic design districts. title: Sohn Fine Art presents group exhibition Sanctuary of Petals
summary: Sohn Fine Art is presenting Sanctuary of Petals, a group exhibition that explores the enduring allure of the natural world through four artists’ visions: Valda Bailey, Edward Merritt, JP Terlizzi, and Hans Withoos. The exhibition invites visitors into a richly imagined botanical sanctuary where flowers communicate through symbols of transformation, memory, and wonder. The featured artists work with mixed media, photography, and unconventional artistic processes. While each artist approaches the floral subject from a unique perspective, together they create an immersive dialogue that celebrates both the beauty and complexity of nature. title: A history of knowledge: The best infographics from the National Geographic archives
summary: Back in the days when the information age was a distant dream and the world a more mysterious place, National Geographic began its mission to reveal the wonders of history, popular science, and culture to eager audiences around the globe. Since that 1888 launch, the world has changed; empires have risen and crumbled and a galaxy of information is today only a click away. But National Geographic endures; its calm, authoritative voice is as respected as ever amid the surfeit of data in our daily lives. In this new anthology, TASCHEN and National Geographic gather the magazine’s best infographics of the past 128 years. Through seven sections—History, The Planet, Being Human, Animal World, World of Plants, Science & Technology, and Space—we encounter the rise and fall of the Roman Empire, the mysterious origins of the Easter Island statues, Cleopatra’s Alexandria, and the anatomy behind a cheetah’s extraordinary speed. title: Irish Museum of Modern Art opens major European exhibition on the concept of peace
summary: The Irish Museum of Modern Art presents Technologies of Peace: Art and Transition in Contemporary Europe (1989–2026), a speculative exhibition bringing together researchers, artists, thinkers, and curators from across Europe to critically examine one of the defining challenges of our time: the question of peace. At a moment marked by ongoing wars, geopolitical instability, social fragmentation, and the constant circulation of conflict through media and culture, conflict is frequently aestheticised, analysed, and consumed. Peace, by contrast, is rarely afforded the same sustained attention. Yet it is precisely now amid escalating global tensions and deepening uncertainty that the complexity, fragility, and transformative potential of peace is asserted. Drawing on artistic, political, and social perspectives across Europe, including Greece, Poland, Romania, Spain, Cyprus, Portugal, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, UK, Kosovo, and Croatia, the exh

title: Monumental Medici bronzes shine again after conservation at Florence's Chapel of the Princes
summary: Two towering bronze portraits of the Medici grand dukes Ferdinando I and Cosimo II have emerged renewed from an extensive conservation campaign at Florence’s Medici Chapels, bringing fresh clarity to works that have watched over the spectacular Chapel of the Princes for centuries. The Museo delle Cappelle Medicee announced the completion of conservation and extraordinary maintenance on the monumental sculptures, together with a new presentation of historic reliquaries formerly displayed in the Medici Crypt. Standing more than three meters high above the grand ducal cenotaphs, the bronzes form part of one of Florence’s most ambitious expressions of Medici power. The Chapel of the Princes, wrapped in elaborate expanses of colored marble and semi-precious stone, was conceived as a dynastic monument to the family that dominated Florentine political and cultural life for generations. title: Yale University Art Gallery opens the first exhibition devoted to the art of the Nguni diaspora
summary: On September 11, 2026, the Yale University Art Gallery opened Nguni: Migrant Nations of Southeast Africa, the first exhibition to situate Nguni artistic traditions within the broader cultural, political, and ecological world that shaped them. Curated by James Green, the Frances and Benjamin Benenson Foundation Associate Curator of African Art at the Gallery, the exhibition features rare loans from South Africa and other national and international institutions as well as works from the Gallery’s own collection. Displayed alongside these masterworks are new commissions by leading contemporary artists, offering a sweeping portrait of Nguni-speaking communities. The works on view reveal how Nguni art emerged from a world defined by cattle pastoralism, deep connections to landscape and lineage, and long-standing networks of cultural interaction.

title: New exhibition exploring 70 Years of The Cavern Club's musical legacy coming to Museum of Liverpool
summary: A new blockbuster exhibition, 70 Years of The Cavern Club will open at Museum of Liverpool on Saturday 16 January 2027 - 70 years to the day since the Cavern opened. Created in collaboration with The Cavern Club, the exhibition charts the club’s journey from a post-war jazz club in a Mathew Street cellar to a global cultural phenomenon and thriving live music venue synonymous with the city. At its heart are the people who have shaped the Cavern across seven decades - from the performers to the fans. Their stories are brought to life through rare photographs, instruments, personal objects and memorabilia that capture the relationships and moments behind its remarkable history. The Cavern Club began life in 1957 as a jazz cellar, but it did not stay one for long. title: Maurizio Cattelan opens major solo exhibition NIGHT at Neue Nationalgalerie in Berlin
summary: Preis der Nationalgalerie 2026 at Neue Nationalgalerie presents NIGHT, the first major solo exhibition in Germany by Italian artist Maurizio Cattelan (born 1960 in Padua). The exhibition brings together seminal works from across Cattelan’s practice with new commissions conceived specifically for Mies van der Rohe’s iconic building. With the new work Purgatory (2026), the exhibition introduces a scaled-down Brandenburg Gate inside the museum, repositioning one of Germany’s most recognizable monuments as a space of passage, reflection, and historical ambiguity. From this point, the exhibition unfolds as a sequence of encounters between bodies, objects, images, and architectural forms. At the centre of the exhibition, Him (2001), Cattelan’s kneeling male figure, is positioned in direct relation to Dawn (2007), a female figure crucified inside a transport crate. title: Supercars and blue-chip classics head to RM Sotheby's Zurich Sale
summary: RM Sotheby’s will host an outstanding boutique sale of 18 exceptional cars at Zurich’s Park Hyatt hotel on 26 September. With the latest in modern hypercars, and a selection of the world’s most desirable supercars, through to stunning examples of blue-chip classics of the 1960s and 70s, the auction will kick-start RM Sotheby’s calendar of live autumn sales. Few cars can claim to have garnered more attention over the past 40 years than the iconic Ferrari F40. Offered in Zurich an example delivered new to Switzerland in July 1991 in the desirable “cat, non-adjust” specification. The car retains its matching-numbers V-8 engine and gearbox and is presented in its factory-correct colour pairing of Rosso Corsa over Stoffa Vigogna. title: Esther Schipper hosts David Claerbout's second solo exhibition in Berlin
summary: Esther Schipper Berlin is presenting a solo exhibition by David Claerbout, the artist’s second with the gallery. Under the title Repose, the exhibition presents four works shown for the first time in Berlin: The woodcarver and the forest, 2025, Birdcage, 2023, Backwards Growing Tree, 2023, and Eagle Eye, 2026. Alongside the videos, a number of works on paper will be exhibited. All films on view explore our relationship to nature and the way we have learned to see the world around us. In The woodcarver and the forest we watch a woodcarver whittling down wooden blocks to create one spoon after another; the act appears almost meditative, until we realize every gesture comes at a cost: outside his window, the forest is slowly being reduced to the objects he creates. title: Eugenio Viola appointed director of Madre Museum
summary: Fondazione Donnaregina per le arti contemporanee – museo Madre announces the appointment of Eugenio Viola as Director, a role he took on in August 2026. Located in the historic centre of Naples, Madre is the Campania Region’s museum of contemporary art and a key institution in Italy’s contemporary art landscape. Through exhibitions, commissions, research, public programs, and its collection, Madre connects artistic practices with the cultural and political issues shaping the present, while maintaining a strong international outlook. Viola returns to Madre after a decade of work throughout Europe, Australia, and Latin America. From 2019 to 2026 he was Artistic Director and Chief Curator of MAMBO–Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá, Colombia; he previously served as Senior Curator at PICA–Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts, Australia (2017–19). title: A new gallery is opening its doors in Brussels to kick off the new art season
summary: To mark the start of the new art season, a new gallery is enriching the Brussels art scene. Ars Belga – Matthu – Boghossian is opening at 2 Rue Saint-Georges, in the heart of the neighborhood of the same name and right next to the Xavier Hufkens Gallery. To inaugurate this new space, the gallery has chosen to bring together two major figures of abstract art: Piero Dorazio and Charles Pollock. This inaugural exhibition immediately affirms Ars Belga’s identity and its ambition: to foster a dialogue among artists, generations, and sensibilities that have shaped the history of modern and contemporary art. Located at 2 Rue Saint-Georges in Brussels, Ars Belga organizes a program of curated exhibitions and participates in major international art fairs, including Abu Dhabi Art, Art Genève, and BRAFA. title: Everyone is talking about Greenland. Eight artists speak for themselves
summary: Copenhagen Contemporary opened its doors to Fire & Ice – On Belonging and Becoming in Kalaallit Nunaat (Greenland), a group exhibition bringing together eight contemporary artists who live, work or have roots in Kalaallit Nunaat, Greenland. The exhibition presents both established artists and a new generation of talent. Across visual art, performance, literature and activism, the artists insist on telling their own stories — at a time when Greenland occupies more of the world's attention than ever, yet is rarely given the floor to speak for itself. The majority of the works are newly commissioned, created specifically for Fire & Ice. This makes the exhibition eight answers to what it means to be connected to Kalaallit Nunaat in 2026 — not as a look back, but as a living interpretation of the present. title: Joana Hadjithomas and Khalil Joreige present research-based exhibition with MAMCO
summary: To decipher the world we live in, artists and filmmakers Joana Hadjithomas & Khalil Joreige (both born in 1969 in Beirut) have elaborated over the last decades a multimedia, research-based practice that confronts the real with the power of image-making, fiction, and poetry. With the works presented here—Palimpsests, Time Capsules, and Trilogies—, Hadjithomas & Joreige investigate the ways visual art give significance to realities that have long remained out of sight. Drawing on geological methodologies and collaborations with practitioners of rescue archaeology, the artists propose representations challenging the writing of history, the visuality of the invisible, and the vertigo induced by deep time. title: Cirkeline turns 70 as Nivaagaards Malerisamling revisits Hanne Hastrup's beloved little elf
summary: It began with a bored 17-year-old, a few circles drawn on paper and a tiny figure that would eventually become one of Denmark’s most enduring children’s characters. In 2027, Cirkeline turns 70, and Nivaagaards Malerisamling will mark the anniversary with an exhibition devoted to Hanne Hastrup’s original drawings and the imaginative world that grew from them. Opening April 10 and running through August 22, Cirkeline har fødselsdag — Cirkeline Has a Birthday — will bring together a broad selection of Hastrup’s drawings alongside a creative workshop and a nature school in the museum’s park. The exhibition is conceived for adults as well as children, giving longtime admirers a chance to revisit a character many first encountered decades ago while introducing her quiet, whimsical universe to a new generation. title: Paris exhibition explores collective creation and intellectual disability in Art Brut
summary: What happens to Art Brut when the idea of the solitary, isolated outsider artist gives way to collaboration, exchange and community? That question lies at the heart of Art Brut ressourcé, a major exhibition bringing the work and philosophy of Belgium’s La “S” Grand Atelier to Halle Saint-Pierre in Paris from September 11, 2026 through July 31, 2027. The exhibition brings together work produced within La “S” Grand Atelier in Vielsalm, Belgium, a center where artists with intellectual disabilities work alongside contemporary artists in residence. title: New Museum elects new members to Board of Trustees
summary: James-Keith Brown, President of the New Museum’s Board of Trustees, and Massimiliano Gioni, Toby Devan Lewis Director of the New Museum, today announced the appointment of ten new members to the Board of Trustees: Donald Capoccia, Christina Hribar, Adriane Iann, Ambassador Randi Levine, Jennifer Levitt, Liza Mauer, Debbie Rechler, Juliana Siqueira de Sá, Sara Story, and Lisa Watson. “As we enter a new era for the New Museum in our recently opened, OMA-designed building expansion, we are delighted to welcome to the Board of Trustees these exceptional individuals who bring broad experience and global perspectives aligning with the New Museum’s mission,” said James-Keith Brown, President of the New Museum’s Board of Trustees. “There is so much excitement around the New Museum, as the momentum

title: Art Gallery of New South Wales opens Dobell Australian Drawing Biennial 2026
summary: Eleven contemporary artists from across Australia feature in the Dobell Australian Drawing Biennial 2026, the country’s leading curated exhibition dedicated to contemporary drawing, opening tomorrow at the Art Gallery of New South Wales. Titled Near at Hand, the exhibition explores drawing as an intimate art form, showcasing personal mark-making, inner imaginings and up-close observations of the everyday. Working across a diverse range of materials including pastel, pencil, watercolour, ceramic, light and thread, the artists in the exhibition reveal innovative approaches and techniques to one of the world's oldest art forms, demonstrating the vitality and evolving possibilities of drawing today. title: Major Kunsthaus Zürich show brings Monet, Picasso, and Tinguely into new dialogues
summary: Monet, Hodler, Picasso, Taeuber-Arp and Tinguely: ‘Evergreens. Selected Works from the Collection’, which runs from 11 September 2026 to 10 January 2027, offers a fresh new take on some of the most important artists at the Kunsthaus Zürich. Masterpieces leave behind their familiar contexts within the Collection and appear in new juxtapositions that open up surprising new perspectives. In wall texts, people from Zurich – including some well-known faces – explain why they chose a particular work as their favourite, and why it moves, remains with or inspires them. Claude Monet’s water lilies, Andy Warhol’s ‘Big Torn Campbell’s Soup Can (Vegetable Beef)’, Franz Gertsch’s ‘Franz and Luciano’, Arnold Böcklin’s ‘Saint Anthony Preaching to the Fish’ and Francis Bacon’s monumental triptych are just some of the highlights from the Kunsthaus Zürich that are

title: New York State Museum marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 with new exhibition, artifacts & programs
summary: The New York State Museum opened a new photography exhibition, a new display of rarely seen artifacts, and a series of public programs to mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center. Together, these exhibitions and programs honor the lives lost, those who responded, and the lasting impact on New York and the nation. Witness to 9/11 is a new photography exhibition that explores the immediate response and aftermath of the attacks, told primarily through the work of two New York Daily News photographers, Todd Maisel and David Handschuh. Both were among the journalists who responded to Lower Manhattan that morning, unaware of what would unfold. In addition to documenting the attacks, Maisel assisted when Handschuh was seriously injured in the collapse of the South Tower.

title: REDCAT presents Flesh Witness examining militarism across Asia and the Pacific
summary: Flesh Witness brings together contemporary artists whose work examines global histories and ongoing conditions of militarism across Asia and the Pacific. Focusing on the Korean Peninsula, Okinawa, the Philippines, Hawai‘i, and Samoa, the group exhibition examines how military power is inscribed in landscapes, bodies, and archives. Flesh Witness includes artworks spanning from the 1970s to newly created work, ranging from video to sculpture, photography, mixed media, and installation. On view from September 12 to December 13, the exhibition features the work of Bernice Akamine, Lani Asunción, Pelenakeke Brown, Crystal Z Campbell, Jisoo Chung, Sean Connelly, Kyuri Jeon, Jane Jin Kaisen, Mao Ishikawa, Slow Futures Laboratory, and Stephanie Syjuco. title: Markus Saile debuts large-scale abstract paintings in solo show at Mai 36
summary: Markus Saile’s second solo exhibition at Mai 36 presents, for the first time, large-scale works that touch upon, and at times almost exceed, the dimensions of the human body and the associated function of the painting as a counterpart to it. The colours of the paintings unfold as a spatial dramaturgy: green and yellow each shape their own rooms, while blue works set distinct accents within the constellations of the exhibition. Through the arrangements and intervals of the architecture-related installation, specific correspondences emerge between the paintings, activating viewers and inviting them to set their gaze in motion and forge connections. A large-scale painting in a pale, yellow ground (Untitled), like several other works in the exhibition, presents an indeterminate monochrome field.
